targets.50: Target AE No Players or Pets

3.assertion: Two buffs carrying SPA 3 both land, but only one value applies: the one furthest from zero on the side of zero it is already on. Among positive values that is the largest; among negative values it is the most negative.

evidence.summary: Reported from play: run-speed buffs do not add. Selo's Accelerating Canto (SPA 3 slot 1) and Flight of Eagles (SPA 3 slot 2) hold at once — different slots, so no arbitration conflict — and having both is no faster than the better one alone.
evidence.source: Reported directly to this project, August 2026

evidence.summary: EQEmu contradicts this: it ADDS movement speed rather than keeping the larger — `newbon->movementspeed += base_value;` — and leaves the comment "should we let these stack?" beside a commented-out highest-wins alternative. The emulator is openly unsure, which is why this is recorded as a disagreement rather than either side being accepted.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/bonuses.cpp, the MovementSpeed case

11.assertion: Two buffs carrying SPA 11 both land, but only one value applies: the one furthest from zero on the side of zero it is already on. Among positive values that is the largest; among negative values it is the most negative. A slow is not a small haste: while any slow is applied no haste applies at all, so a negative value takes this slot outright.

evidence.summary: Reported from play: two SPA 11 hastes do not add. The highest applies and the rest do nothing while all of them are up. A slow is not a smaller haste — while any slow is on you no SPA 11 haste applies at all.
evidence.source: Reported directly to this project, August 2026

evidence.summary: SPA 11 is the ordinary spell haste every raid carries. Keeps the larger value: `if ((effect_value - 100) > new_bonus->haste) new_bonus->haste = effect_value - 100;`. Accumulated into its own `haste` field, separate from the two other haste types, and never added to another SPA 11 buff. Found the same way as the other entries here — a spell-bonus path that keeps the larger magnitude where an ordinary bonus uses +=. It was missed on the first pass because haste is handled in a different switch from the effects that produced the rest of this list.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/bonuses.cpp, ApplySpellsBonuses — the AttackSpeed, AttackSpeed2 and AttackSpeed3 cases. No commit message or source cited for the behaviour, as with the rest of this list.

98.assertion: Two buffs carrying SPA 98 both land, but only one value applies: the one furthest from zero on the side of zero it is already on. Among positive values that is the largest; among negative values it is the most negative. A slow is not a small haste: while any slow is applied no haste applies at all, so a negative value takes this slot outright.

evidence.summary: SPA 98 is bard haste. Keeps the larger value into `hastetype2`, which EQEmu's own comment describes as "Stacks with V1 but does not Overcap" — a separate bucket from SPA 11 that adds to it, while two SPA 98 buffs do not add to each other.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/bonuses.cpp, ApplySpellsBonuses — the AttackSpeed, AttackSpeed2 and AttackSpeed3 cases. No commit message or source cited for the behaviour, as with the rest of this list.

focus-best-only/all-focus-spas.assertion: When more than one focus effect could apply to the same cast, only the best one applies — they do not add. The exceptions are the proc-type foci (339 TriggerOnCast, 340 SpellTrigger, 383 SympatheticProc), which fire independently and can all land on one cast.

evidence.summary: 'The only ones where the effects actually can work on the same spell are SPA 383 and SPA 340, all other foci are best works only... I guess 339 too.'
evidence.source: Feedback on the project, 2026-08-21

evidence.summary: Daybreak's list names 339 Fc_CastProc and 383 Fc_CastProcNormalized — the two proc-type foci reported as able to fire together are, in the publisher's own naming, the cast-proc focus family. 340 is named Chance Spell and is not a focus at all, which is why it never enters the best-only set.
evidence.source: Daybreak's enumerated SPA list, https://forums.daybreakgames.com/eq/index.php?threads/enumerated-spa-list.206288/ (kept verbatim at tools/reference/daybreak-spa-list.txt)

evidence.summary: EQEmu's focus aggregation keeps the best rather than summing: `if (Total > 0 && realTotal >= 0 && Total > realTotal) realTotal = Total;` across the item, AA and spell buckets. Procs are routed separately through focusSympatheticProc and focusTriggerOnCast, matching the three named exceptions exactly.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/spell_effects.cpp Mob::GetFocusEffect and zone/bonuses.cpp:4157,4167

focus-stacking/not-on-client-ignore-list.assertion: Focus effects stack regardless of slot conflicts. Most focus SPAs are already exempt from slot arbitration, but some are missing from the client-derived ignore list the engine uses, so the tool may report a conflict between two focus buffs that in fact coexist.

evidence.summary: Focus SPAs — the Fc_ entries in Daybreak's enumerated SPA list — stack regardless of slot conflicts.
evidence.source: Feedback on the project, 2026-08-21, citing Daybreak's enumerated SPA list

evidence.summary: Daybreak's own list names 81 SPAs with an Fc_ or Ff_ prefix, so which effects are focus effects is published rather than inferred. It establishes the category, not the stacking behaviour — but it is a superset of what EQEmu treats as focus, naming every one of those and three more (212, 497, 528).
evidence.source: Daybreak's enumerated SPA list, https://forums.daybreakgames.com/eq/index.php?threads/enumerated-spa-list.206288/ (kept verbatim at tools/reference/daybreak-spa-list.txt)

evidence.summary: Of the 44 SPAs EQEmu treats as focus effects, 31 are already on the stacking ignore list, so the category is plainly meant to be exempt and the rest look like gaps. SPA 460 Ff_Override_NotFocusable is in EQEmu's own IsFocusLimit() but missing from IsEffectIgnoredInStacking() — an internal inconsistency. The list's tail is self-described as guesswork: 'Spell effects implemented after ROF2, following same pattern, lets assume these should go here.'
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server common/spdat.cpp IsEffectIgnoredInStacking and IsFocusLimit

evidence.summary: The folk belief that twincast effects 'do not stack' looked like a counterexample for SPA 399, since it sits below the ignore list's ceiling. It is not: two twincast buffs do both hold, and only the best twincast chance applies to a cast — which is the focus_best_only rule, not a stacking conflict. Recorded because the distinction is the thing people get wrong.
evidence.source: Long-standing player report, reconciled against the focus_best_only claim

stacking-rule/slot-arbitration.assertion: Two buffs conflict only where the same SPA sits in the same slot index; the same effect in different slots does not conflict.

evidence.summary: Daybreak, describing the reworked spell critical damage effect: "All modifiers stack (assuming they are in different slots)." Stated as a property of the slot system rather than of that one effect, and the only public statement of it by Daybreak found so far. Corroborated by their own patch practice: the 11 February 2026 update notes fix stacking conflicts by moving effects between slot indexes — "Moved the Strength debuff in the Grip of Mori DoT line from slot 2 to slot 5 to avoid stacking conflicts."
evidence.source: Daybreak, EverQuest news, "July Patch Cliff Notes", 23 July 2015 — https://www.everquest.com/news/july-patch-cliff-notes

evidence.summary: Dzarn, on why SPA 416 duplicates SPA 1: "SPA 416 functions exactly like SPA 1, it was added so that we could avoid stacking conflicts with only 12 spell slots." Same behaviour under a different SPA number to escape a conflict, which only makes sense if a conflict needs a shared effect within the slots. It explains a pattern visible across the dataset: AC_2 (416), Skill Damage Mod 2 (459), Skill Min_Damage Amt 2 (418) and Contact Ability 2 (419) are all duplicates that exist to dodge one. Rated below primary for two reasons: it presupposes the rule rather than stating it, and it reaches us through a third party transcribing a thread that no longer serves to readers, so the wording has not been checked against the original post.
evidence.source: Dzarn, quoted in rumstil/eqspellparser core/SpellData.cs case 416 (May 2014), citing https://forums.daybreakgames.com/eq/index.php?threads/ac-vs-acv2.210028/

evidence.summary: CheckStackConflict compares effect ids at matching slot indexes, so the same SPA in different slots never collides.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/spells.cpp Mob::CheckStackConflict

stacking-rule/slot-strength.assertion: Where two buffs do share a slot, the incoming spell must be at least as strong on every shared slot or it is refused outright; if it is stronger it overwrites.

evidence.summary: The comparison half of CheckStackConflict: a slot-by-slot loop that rejects the incoming spell the moment any shared slot is weaker. Split out from slot-arbitration when Daybreak was found to have stated the slot-index rule but not this one — nothing outside EQEmu establishes the all-or-nothing refusal.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/spells.cpp Mob::CheckStackConflict

bonus-bucket/slow-cancels-haste.assertion: A slow does not average with a haste, and is not treated as a smaller one. While any slow is applied, no haste applies at all — the haste is removed rather than reduced.

evidence.summary: Reported from play: applying any slow removes the haste entirely rather than netting the two off against each other.
evidence.source: Reported directly to this project, August 2026

evidence.summary: EQEmu behaves the same way, in two places. A haste is refused outright while the spell haste bonus is already negative — `if (new_bonus->haste < 0) break; // Slowed - Don’t apply haste` — and once slowed, the haste calculation returns before item haste, SPA 98 or SPA 119 are added to it, under the comment "slow beats all! Besides a better inhibit".
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/bonuses.cpp ApplySpellsBonuses (AttackSpeed, AttackSpeed2) and zone/client_mods.cpp Client::CalcHaste

bonus-bucket/haste-types-add.assertion: SPA 119 is overhaste: a separate bucket from the SPA 11 melee haste, which adds on top of it rather than competing with it. Within either bucket they do not add — the highest applies.

evidence.summary: The client's own descriptions say it twice over. Battlecry of the Vah Shir (#2606), an SPA 119 song: "This increase is cumulative with most other effects that increase attack speed." And the name of the mechanic is in the text of the effects that carry it — Frenzied Burnout I (#2754) reads "increases ... overhaste by 15%". Of the 152 spells in the current file whose description uses the word overhaste, 152 carry SPA 119 and none carries SPA 371.
evidence.source: dbstr_us.txt, shipped with the live client

evidence.summary: Reported from play: an SPA 11 haste and an SPA 119 haste both count, where two of the same kind do not.
evidence.source: Reported directly to this project, August 2026

evidence.summary: EQEmu accumulates them into separate fields and then sums those fields — `h += spellbonuses.haste` and, subject to its own cap, `h += spellbonuses.hastetype3`. Each field keeps only its own largest value.
evidence.source: EQEmu/Server zone/client_mods.cpp Client::CalcHaste, and zone/bonuses.cpp for the per-field accumulation

bonus_buckets.lead: For every non-cumulative claim the rule is the same: the larger value wins within one bonus bucket. What follows is where that comes from, and what it does not cover.

blocks.title: There is more than one bucket
blocks.body: EQEmu sums the spell, AA and worn-item buckets at use time. Best-only applies inside each bucket, and the three totals then add. Two buffs — the case this tool compares — are both in the spell bucket, which is why one of them is wasted.
blocks.caveat: 185, 459, 482, 503 and 505 are additive when they arrive as a worn item bonus rather than as a buff.

blocks.title: Daybreak names the mechanic
blocks.quote: Only the best modifier from AAs was added, and only the best modifier from spells was added
blocks.body: “Best only” is Daybreak’s own term for it, and the page confirms the buckets are separate and each best-only.
blocks.caveat: It describes spell critical damage being changed *away* from that behaviour, so it does not speak to the seven SPAs listed here.

blocks.title: A developer describes the same shape
blocks.quote: For stacking, Base1 is cumulative while Base2 takes the highest value between spells or AAs.
blocks.source: relayed by rumstil/eqspellparser, core/SpellData.cs case 219, added November 2016
blocks.body: Cumulative and highest-wins sitting in one effect, split across its two values, with the highest taken per bucket. That is independent of the 2015 patch notes and says the buckets are real.
blocks.caveat: It is about SPA 219 rather than the seven listed here, and it is a relay rather than the original post.

blocks.title: Haste shows why this list is not one pool
blocks.body: SPA 11 and SPA 119 each keep only their own largest value, but they accumulate into separate fields that DO add to each other — EQEmu’s own comments call 98 "Stacks with V1 but does not Overcap" and 119 "Stacks and Overcaps". Two SPA 11 hastes do not add; an SPA 11 and an SPA 119 do. That is why overlaps are reported per SPA here and never merged across them.
blocks.caveat: Haste is also the one place a bonus and a penalty have a settled answer. A slow is not a small haste: while any slow is applied no haste applies at all, so a negative value takes the slot outright. Everywhere else, two values on opposite sides of zero name nobody. See bonus-bucket/slow-cancels-haste and bonus-bucket/haste-types-add.

claim_notes.movement_and_mounts: Movement speed has an exception this tool cannot see. A mount overrides a player's movement buff outright rather than the larger of the two winning — Spirit of Wolf is overwritten by Knight's Holy Steed regardless of values. It is not modelled here and could not be: Holy Steed carries only SPA 113 (SummonMount) and no SPA 3 at all, so a mount's speed is not expressed in the spell file. Reported by Matrim, August 2026. If you compare a run buff against a mount here you will be told they do not share an effect, which is true of the spell data and not of the game.
